learningObjective: Set up object replication between storage accounts, meet what it needs first, and explain how it's different from geo-redundant storage.
engineer: What it needs first: blob versioning on both accounts; change feed on the source account; no hierarchical namespace (Data Lake accounts don't work).
What it copies: block blobs only. Blobs in the Archive tier are not copied.

The replication policy: it holds rules. Each rule says: from this source container, to this destination container, optionally only blobs starting with a prefix, and whether to copy existing blobs too or only new ones. With the API or CLI, create the policy on the destination first, then on the source.
Timing: copying happens in the background, with no guaranteed time (no SLA). Each blob on the source shows its replication status: Complete or Failed.
Destination is read-only: while the policy exists, you can't write to the copied blobs in the destination container.
Other tenants: copying to an account in another Entra tenant is blocked by default on new accounts (AllowCrossTenantReplication = false).

When to use it: faster reads for users in another region; processing data in another region, close to the compute; sending data to several accounts; saving money by copying to an account on a cheaper tier.

example.title: Analytics in another region
body: Sales uploads data to stweu in West Europe. The analytics cluster runs in North Europe. Object replication copies the reports container to stneu, so the cluster reads it locally.
Only blobs starting with 'final/' are copied, so unfinished files stay where they are.

architectureDecisions: Pick the right tool: object replication to put data near users or compute; GRS or GZRS to survive the loss of a region.
Filter by prefix: copy only finished data, so you pay for less.

misconceptions.myth: Object replication is a disaster-recovery feature like GRS, with failover.
misconceptions.reality: No. There is no failover. It just copies containers in the background.
No. Only block blobs, and not ones in the Archive tier.

comparisons.difference: GRS copies the whole account to the fixed paired region, and you can only read the copy with RA-. Object replication copies chosen containers to any account in any region, and the destination is a normal account you can read.
Very similar: it also needs versioning and copies by bucket and prefix.
AzCopy copies when you run it or schedule it. Object replication copies all the time, and Azure runs it for you.

troubleshooting.symptom: You can't create the replication rule.
troubleshooting.cause: Versioning or change feed isn't on, or the account has hierarchical namespace.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn on what's needed, and use an account without hierarchical namespace.

troubleshooting.symptom: Some blobs show replication status Failed.
troubleshooting.cause: For example, the blob is archived, or the destination container is missing.
troubleshooting.fix: Rehydrate the blob or fix the destination. Check the status on each blob.

troubleshooting.symptom: The app can't write to the destination container.
troubleshooting.fix: Write to the source instead, or remove the policy.

troubleshooting.symptom: Copying to a partner's tenant fails.
troubleshooting.fix: Allow cross-tenant replication on both accounts, if your rules permit it.

configuration.limits: Destination blobs are read-only while the policy exists
configuration.permissions: Storage Account Contributor on both accounts
